item.title: Re: The UK’s recruitment for foundation medicine does NOT require radical reform
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Waiting to be told where you are going to work in August is stressful, and we should aim to get allocations to the students as early as possible. However this does not need radical reform. The system in position previously used the SJT an exam that was both racist and sexist (FY1 SJT Technical Report [1]) and had absolutely no foundation in merit. item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor We welcome discussion of the ethical dimensions of our planned randomised trial evaluating the health effects of hepatitis B vaccination at birth in Guinea-Bissau. item.title: Prebunking may protect trust better than constant debunking in routine patient communication
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Morgan’s mermaid (1) is a helpful methafor for clinicians because it shifts attention from the content of a falsehood to the craft that makes it persuasive. The illusory truth effect is not a niche laboratory curiosity; repetition changes perceived truth even when people “know better,” which should temper the instinct to rebut every claim in real time (2). item.title: Re: Oral ivermectin versus 5% permethrin cream to treat children and adults with classic scabies: multicentre, assessor blinded, cluster randomised clinical trial
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor We read with interest the article by Boralevi et al. that established the superiority in the treatment of classic scabies of 5% permethrin cream compared to oral ivermectin. item.title: Re: Scrutiny of the assisted dying bill is vital but obstruction in the House of Lords could mean it never becomes law
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor I have been engaged in the assisted dying debate for many years, and I believe there are parallels between the errors the medical profession has made in its handling of this issue and the apparent failure of the House of Lords to scrutinise the assisted dying bill effectively, as highlighted by Hayter et al. Others may remember the furore over the Royal Colleges’ and BMA’s reasonable decisions to survey their members to inform their policies on assisted dying
